(p. 99)

**Sūrat al-Taghābun**

Its purpose is to deliver a clear warning against what the hypocrites were warned about, by establishing a decisive proof that it is among the matters presented for judgment, down to the smallest speck, on the Day of Resurrection, the Day of the Great Gathering. Its name, al-Taghābun (Mutual Loss and Gain), makes this meaning clear, and it is the most explicit indication of this within the surah. For this reason it is named accordingly.

**﴿Bismillāh﴾** (In the name of Allah), the Owner of dominion, for there is no equal or peer to Him. **﴿al-Raḥmān﴾** (the Most Merciful), whose vast and magnificent goodness encompasses all creation. **﴿al-Raḥīm﴾** (the Most Compassionate), who singled out for special favor a people above those whom His general mercy covers, for their excellence.

* *

When the previous surah was concluded with the affirmation of Allah's dominance through the executed command and the all-encompassing knowledge, this surah opens with the all-encompassing praise and the constant exaltation of Allah above every flaw of deficiency. This guides us to reflect on His actions and to contemplate His creation, for that is the path to knowing Him. As for knowing His essence in reality, it is impossible, since no one knows a thing in that manner except its like, and He has no like. So He says, emphasizing what the opening of Surah al-Jumu'ah had conveyed: **﴿Yusabbiḥu﴾** (glorifies), that is, perfectly declares His transcendence, continuously and constantly, **﴿lillāh﴾** (to Allah), who alone encompasses all the attributes of perfection, **﴿mā fī al-samāwāt﴾** (whatever is in the heavens), which includes the earths and what is in them. Nothing in them wills anything except that it happens in accordance with His will. Thus this existence and all that exists bear witness to His freedom from every flaw of deficiency.

Since the address was with those mentioned at the end of the hypocrites' passage, who need emphasis, He says, emphasizing by repeating the relative pronoun: **﴿wa-mā fī al-arḍ﴾** (and whatever is on the earth), that is, likewise, by their indication of His perfection and self-sufficiency. It has been stated earlier that the obedience of a rational being to a command is like the obedience of a non-rational being to a will. Therefore it is incumbent upon him to refine his soul to the utmost refinement, so that he is obedient to Him by carrying out the commands, just as non-rational beings obey by fulfilling what is willed of them.

When Allah, glory be to Him, presented this transmitted proof of His perfect transcendence in a manner that the rational proof is understood by one who has intellect, as 'Alī (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Heard speech does not benefit if it is not impressed upon the mind, just as the sun does not benefit the eye that is blind." This is because He made them contained creatures, as is observed, and the contained requires the existence of its container before it. Thus it is incapable. So it glorifies Him constantly. If it does not do so with a spoken tongue, it does so with the tongue of its state. Its Maker is free of need of a container, so everything else is in need of glorification. **[He explained]** this by His saying: **﴿Lahu﴾** (To Him alone), that is, **﴿al-mulk﴾** (belongs the dominion), **[that is]** all of it, absolutely, in this world and the next. It is general sovereignty over the particular and the general, and general governance with its two pillars: repelling evils and attracting goods, which bring joy and delight, both through bringing into existence and through annihilating. This is more eloquent than what is in al-Jumu'ah, for dominion may be dominion in form only, and that dominion in which it is apparent to others. The continuous glorification required by the greatness of the King here is greater than that continuity there.

When in al-Jumu'ah the transcendence above deficiency followed, here He follows it with the attribution of perfection, saying: **﴿Wa-lahu﴾** (And to Him alone), that is, **﴿al-ḥamd﴾** (belongs the praise), that is, the encompassing of all attributes of perfection. For this reason all His creatures glorify Him. Whoever understands their glorification is **[the one who does good]**. Whoever has in his nature and original disposition the capacity to understand, but then neglects it, is likely to return and understand. Whoever is not prepared for this is the misguided one for whom there is no remedy. **﴿Wa-huwa﴾** (And He alone is), that is, **﴿ʿalā kull shayʾin﴾** (over every thing), that is, every thing possible for the will to relate to, **﴿qadīr﴾** (All-Powerful), because He alone has knowledge of everything absolutely, since the relation of His essence, which necessitates power, to all things is equal. This is very clear. And because whoever knows himself by his deficiency knows his Lord by perfection and the strength of authority and majesty.

Abū Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr, may Allah have mercy on him, said: When [Allah] expounded in the two surahs the condition of those among the Children of Israel who carried the Torah and then did not carry it, and the condition of the hypocrites who displayed Islam while their hearts were thick with disbelief and obstinacy, and He clarified the departure of the two groups from the straight path and their deviation from the upright religion, and the mention of their attribute of sharing common characteristics implied their particular disbelief with the mark of singularity, a mark that signals the magnitude of that distance, apart from what included the other factions of the disbelievers, Allah, exalted is He, informed [about] the fact that creation in its entirety, though the sects diverge and the paths separate, returns by the rule of precedents to two ways. He, exalted is He, said: **﴿He it is who created you, so among you is a disbeliever and among you is a believer﴾** [al-Taghābun: 2]. We have already explained the proofs that believers are of various ranks, that the people of disbelief are of many levels, and that the hypocrites are the lowest in condition and the worst in disbelief and misguidance: **﴿Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depth of the Fire﴾** [al-Nisā': 145]. The surah opened with transcendence on account of the great offense of the hypocrites in their ignorance. Even if the surah of the Hypocrites contained nothing of their great offense except what Allah, exalted is He, related of their saying: **﴿If we return to Medina, the more honorable will surely expel the more humble﴾** [al-Munāfiqūn: 8], it would suffice. His saying, exalted is He, **﴿He knows what is in the heavens and the earth, and He knows what you conceal and what you declare, and Allah is Knowing of the contents of the breasts﴾** [al-Taghābun: 4], alludes to what precedes and follows it of the verses, concerning the evil ignorance of the hypocrites and the great deprivation in their saying with their tongues what their hearts did not hold: **﴿And Allah testifies that the hypocrites are liars﴾** [al-Munāfiqūn: 1], and their taking their oaths as a shield and their turning people away from the way of Allah, to what He, glory be to Him, described them with. So He, glory be to Him and exalted is He, opened the surah of al-Taghābun by declaring Himself free of what they imagined of their offenses, which are not hidden from Him, glory be to Him: **﴿Do they not know that Allah knows their secret and their private talk?﴾** [al-Tawbah: 78]. Then He said, exalted is He: **﴿and He knows what you conceal and what you declare﴾** [al-Taghābun: 4]. So He rebuked and reproached them in a number of verses. Then He pointed to what prevented them from reflecting on the verses and turned them away from considering the miracles, and that it was arrogance that destroyed others besides them. He, exalted is He, said, informing about their predecessors in this offense, of those whose end was painful punishment and a wretched final abode: **﴿That is because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs, but they said, "Shall mere humans guide us?" So they disbelieved and turned away﴾** [al-Taghābun: 6]. Then the speech was interwoven, identifying their eschatological end and the end of others, up to His saying: **﴿And wretched is the destination﴾** [al-Taghābun: 10]. The connection of what follows will become clear in the commentary, by Allah's power. Finished.

Since the greatest proofs of Him, glory be to Him, are the signs of the horizons, ﴿We shall show them Our signs in the horizons﴾ [Fussilat: 53], and the signs within themselves, and since He placed the first first, in its upper and lower parts, because of its clarity, He followed it with the second as a proof of the comprehensiveness of His power, which indicates the completeness of His dominion, by His being singled out for originating the most wondrous of things in creation and for bearing people up through hardships. So He said: ﴿He is the One who created you﴾, that is, He alone, ﴿who created you﴾, that is, brought you into being in the state you are in, by decreeing you and bringing you into existence in truth, in accordance with the decree. This is contrary to those among the al-Dahriyya (those who deny a Creator and attribute events to time alone) and the People of Nature (ahl al-tabai', those who attribute events to natural dispositions) who denied this.

Since what preceded in Surat al-Munafiqun made known that people are of two groups, this surah recognizes that this division results from His origination of them, because it is customary for a king that among his subjects there are a friend and an enemy, one who agrees and one who opposes, one who obeys and one who disobeys. The king takes revenge, pardons, punishes, rewards, advances, delays, raises, and lowers. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ said: "If you did not sin and then seek forgiveness, God would take you away and bring a people who would sin and then seek forgiveness, and they would be forgiven." Related by Muslim and al-Tirmidhi from Abu Ayyub, may Allah be pleased with him. Then He, exalted is He, said, placing the enemy first as an indication that He knows of it and is able over it, and that nothing of it occurs except by His will. There is also an allusion in it that the enemy is the greater in number, yet despite its multitude it is the weaker, because Allah, exalted is He, is not with it in His support; otherwise He would have annihilated the other category. ﴿So among you﴾, that is, as a consequence of His creating you and His determining your forms, from which your dispositions arise, if it is among you by His origination of your attributes just as He originated your essences, ﴿there is a disbeliever﴾, that is, one deeply rooted in the attribute of disbelief, destroying himself by what He prepared him for in acquisition and facilitated for him after He created him in the best of forms upon the original fitrah (natural disposition). In the hadith, the boy whom al-Khidr, peace be upon him, killed was stamped as a disbeliever. The meaning is that his original fitrah was created prepared for disbelief. Actions are general and specific: the specific ones are attributed to the servant, one says "he prayed, fasted, believed, or disbelieved," and the general ones are attributed to Allah, exalted is He, so one says: He originated the power of motion and rest and the creation of motion and rest. The specific actions are the object of command and prohibition. ﴿And among you is a believer﴾, that is, one firmly established in faith in the judgment of Allah, exalted is He, from eternity, who saves himself through righteous deeds that agree with the eternal knowledge. He, glory be to Him, created the disbeliever and created his disbelief as an act belonging to him, and the believer and his faith as an act belonging to him, because He created the power and the choice and concealed the matter of the outcome. Each of the two writes by his choice according to the decree of Allah, and nothing comes into being from either of them except what He decreed for him and willed from him, because the existence of what is not decreed is incapacity, and the opposite of the known will is ignorance. From this division it is known with certainty that one of the two divisions is false, astray, and opposed to the command of the King whose dominion is established. It is certainly known that every king must judge among his subjects regarding [the matter] over which they differ, and must grant justice to the wronged against his wrongdoer. It is observed that some of them die in their disbelief without any loss befalling them, and some die in their faith likewise. Thus it is known that this abode is not the abode of decision, and that the abode prepared for that is only after death and resurrection. This is something fixed in natural dispositions, and no one is ignorant of it. But creation turned away from it because of what they are engaged in from distractions, so it has become something that does not occur to them in denial, and has reached a state where their intellects cannot independently grasp it. Yet when they are reminded of it, and these distractions which He, glory be to Him, indicated are made clear to them, and they strip the soul of its portions and of its persistence in familiarity, they all count it among the self-evident matters. It is also known from His making their division a consequence of His decree the obligation [of belief] in the decree, its good and its evil.

Since the estimation is: "The One who originated you and carried you upon that, and differentiated among you, is powerful over everything," He followed it with His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Allah﴾, that is, the One who has complete encompassment of this act of His. He placed the prepositional phrase first, not for restriction, but as an indication of greater concern, as when you say to one who asks you, "Do you know such and such?", and it appears from him a hesitation about your knowledge of it: "Yes, I know it, and I know nothing other than it." So He said: ﴿of what you do﴾, that is, what you bring about by way of action as acquisition, ﴿is All-Seeing﴾, that is, of perfect knowledge of that. He is the One who created all your actions, whose acquisition is attributed to you, and He is the Creator of all the capacities and attributes just as He created the essences, contrary to the Qadariyya (those who deny the divine decree and affirm human absolute creative power), because it is inconceivable that the Creator should create what He does not know. If a person were asked how many steps he took in his day, he would not know; how much more so if he were asked where his walking took place and when. Indeed, he walks most of his walking while being unaware of it. Given his ignorance of his actions in quantity, quality, place, and other respects, he is not a creator of them in any way.

When he mentioned the contained, he mentioned its container, indicating His complete encompassing of the inner and the outer, by [saying] that He creates a very great thing, so that it comes out in accordance with His will, and then it needs nothing added to it and nothing taken from it. So He said: ﴿He created the heavens﴾, which are the roof of the house of the King's servants, despite their greatness and height as you see, ﴿and the earth﴾, which is the floor and cradle of their house, despite its vastness and what is in it of conveniences and aids, ﴿in truth﴾, i.e., with the matter to which reality corresponds, neither exceeding it nor falling short. Rather, reality came from it in exact conformity with what He willed, not as one of us wills a thing and then, when he brings it into being, it does not accord with his intention. By the manifestation of the established matter and the nullification of falsehood, He is the creator of the two abodes, the worldly and the otherworldly, contrary to whoever does not say so, such as the Sabians, the philosophers, and others.

When the people of natures (ahl al-ṭabā'i') said that the spheres have an influence by their essence and nature, He said, negating that and reminding them of His blessing so that you may be thankful: ﴿And He shaped you﴾, i.e., you the addressees, in forms that do not correspond to any of the forms of the higher beings or the lower beings, nor is there among them any form that fully corresponds to another in every respect. ﴿Then He made your forms good﴾, so He made them the best forms of all animals, as is observed in this world, and likewise in the Hereafter, contrary to the people of metempsychosis (al-tanāsukh). Moreover, their arrangement in itself is the best of arrangements; if any part of them were moved from its place to something else that we know, ugliness would result. The human being is favored by being adorned with the choicest attributes of created beings. He, glory be to Him, made his limbs operate in every way that the limbs of other animals operate, with additions peculiar to the human being, such as beauty of face and comeliness of the members. Thus he is best in relation to the species as such, and in relation to the individuals in reality, even though some of them are better than others. The ugliness of the ugly is only in relation to what is more beautiful than it. Therefore the sages said: two things have no limit, beauty and eloquence. So He created man in the best stature, which does not negate that the species He made the best of the individual kinds, relative to what is above it in the genus, has no limit to the superiority of some of its members over others. One observes what has been found of the individuals of its species in essences, and the power of Allah is not limited.

Beware of giving ear to what occurred in the books of Imam al-Ghazali, that it is not within possibility to be more originative than what has been. Although he knew that he was objected to in this, and he answered the objection in the book where he answered the things he was objected to, that answer too carries no weight, for it resolves into the claim that He, glory be to Him and exalted, is not able to create anything better than this world, and no one says this. It does not diminish al-Ghazali's standing, for every person's words are taken and rejected, as Imam Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, said. Al-Ghazali himself attributed this to Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them. Imam al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him and content him, said: "I composed these books and spared no effort in them, and I know that in them there is error, because Allah Most High says: ﴿Had it been from other than Allah, they would have found in it much discrepancy﴾ [al-Nisa': 82]."

Since the implication was that the origin was from Him, glory be to Him, He joined to it His saying: ﴿And to Him﴾, i.e., to Him alone, ﴿is the return﴾, i.e., after the resurrection, by the very power with which He determined the beginning. Whoever was upon the original nature and did not alter it, He admits to Paradise. Whoever had corrupted it, making his spirit a breath by what He imprinted in it from the point where He gave it a body, He admits to the Fire. And in this world too, by His sole management, nothing comes from the king or the commoner except what He wills, not what that willer, the doer, wills.

When the preceding discussion established the comprehensiveness of His power, as shown by His originating creation in this firmly ordered form, and when the decisive proof testified that He alone made it, with no action in it by any nature or anything else, this indicated that this is due to the all-encompassing extent of His knowledge. This is an indication that whoever does not have perfect knowledge has deficient power. So He said: ﴿He knows﴾, meaning His knowledge is established in the past, and in the present and the future it relates to the known things according to the way His power relates to them in line with His will, by bringing them into existence. ﴿Whatever﴾, meaning that which, or everything, ﴿in the heavens﴾, all of them.

Since the discourse came after the establishment of the definitive, self-evident proof for all the fundamentals of religion (usul al-din) with the sincere ones, because the self-evidence of the proofs led them to belief, or to a state in which they became fit for belief and adorned with the adornment of the people of rectitude, He did not repeat the relative pronoun but said: ﴿and the earth﴾. Since He mentioned the state of the container in a way that includes what it contains, and since knowing the states of rational beings is more difficult, He said, emphasizing by repeating the governing verb: ﴿and He knows﴾, meaning on the basis of continuity, ﴿what you conceal﴾ (p-110), meaning in solitude and in private with certain individuals. Since their subtlety and dispersal are such that some of the weak deny that He comprehends them, and since open declaration may be obscured by a great deal of noise, confusion of voices, and the like, He emphasized and said: ﴿and what you declare﴾, both universals and particulars. This is against those who say that He knows only universals [alone] and does not know particulars [except] after they come into existence, whether philosophers or others, and against those who say: He knows only universals in particular.

Since He mentioned the state of the contained in a way that includes its containers, which are the breasts (al-sudur), and since their matter is more wondrous than that of others, He stated them explicitly, indicating the subtlety of their matter, and placed the apparent noun where a pronoun would be, for glorification: ﴿And Allah﴾, meaning the One to whom belongs complete comprehensiveness of every perfection, ﴿is All-Knowing﴾, meaning of utmost knowledge, ﴿of what is within the breasts﴾, meaning the possessors of the breasts, of secrets and thoughts that have not been brought out into the external world, whether the possessor of the breast knows them or not. His knowledge of all of that is equal, with no difference between knowledge of the hidden and knowledge of the manifest, because the relation of what requires His knowledge, which is the existence of His essence as it is with the attributes of perfection, to all things is equal. So be watchful of Him in sincerity and in other matters, with the watchfulness of one who knows that He is truly not absent from him, and beware lest your secret differ from your open conduct, for it is due to Him that you should be wary and cautious. The repetition of knowledge in this sense (p-111) corresponds to the repetition of the warning. The mention of the establishment of power precedes the establishment of knowledge, because the created things point to His power primarily and essentially, and the perfection of His power entails the perfection of His knowledge, since whoever does not perfect his knowledge does not complete his power, and so would not produce a creation firmly ordered.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 64, verse 5:

When the belief in Him was established, namely that He is the King to whom alone belongs true kingship, and He indicated, by what is observed of the division of His servants into believer and disbelievER, that it is not befitting, neither in wisdom nor in custom, to take the hand of the wrongdoer from either of them, as is the practice of kings, and He informed that His knowledge encompasses all things, since it relates equally to the higher and lower realms, and to the outward and the inward, He followed this with the obligation of believing in His messengers, in order to unite the word upon Him, glorified is He, so that life may be completed through the reconciliation of relations, lest discord occur and corrupt life, and with the obligation of taking heed of those nations that passed before them. Whoever does not take heed stumbles upon his own desire through hope. He pointed to this by destroying those who opposed them with a destruction arranged in orderly fashion, in breach of the customary course and with its particularity to them, in a manner established as a past matter, showing from His sole possession of the kingdom that the disbelievers are the falsifiers. So He said: ﴿Has there not come to you﴾, that is, O people, and especially the disbelievers, so that you may know that He is all-encompassing in knowledge and all-enveloping in power, who takes vengeance upon the evildoer, ﴿the news of those who﴾, and He expressed it in a manner that includes the severe and the weak of disbelief, saying: ﴿disbelieved﴾, that is, their great account.

Since those who were destroyed in that manner were some of the disbelievers, namely those to whom messengers were sent, and they did not encompass all the time that had passed, He said: ﴿before﴾ (p-112) like the generations mentioned in al-A'raf. Then He attributed to their disbelief, and followed His words: ﴿so they tasted﴾, that is, they experienced the experience of one who tastes, with the second justice, just as He had judged against them with the first justice by dividing them into disbeliever and believer, ﴿the evil consequence of their affair﴾, that is, the severity of what they were in, which deserves to be consulted about, commanded and forbidden, and its heaviness and the unwholesomeness of its pasture in this world; its origin is heaviness, however it is inverted. ﴿And for them﴾, that is, in addition to what they tasted because of it in this world, ﴿is a painful punishment﴾ in the barzakh, then in the Resurrection, which is the place of the greatest separation.

When He (glorified be He) mentioned what He had visited upon them, and indicated with certainty that it came from Him, through His consistent breaking of customary patterns, with annihilation and special punishment for those who denied the messengers and deliverance for those who affirmed them, He gave the reason in His saying: ﴿That﴾, i.e., the matter, the monstrous and great calamity, which decisively shows that disbelief is the most false of falsehoods and that it is something that angers the Creator. Since its purpose is not like the purpose of Ghafir (the Forgiver), in dividing people into two categories, and their division here came only incidentally, to point to the Hour, He suffices with the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-sha'n, the dummy or "pronoun of the matter" in grammar) and said: ﴿Because﴾, i.e., because of the fact that the matter, great and extremely dreadful, ﴿their messengers used to come to them﴾ as a continuous habit, ﴿their messengers﴾, i.e., the messengers of God whom He sent to them and singled out for them, so that they would be the object of their joy, ﴿with the clear proofs﴾, i.e., matters that make extremely clear that they were messengers of God, from books and other things, so they witnessed the matter from its source. Therefore their punishment was more severe.

(p-113) Since Glorified and Exalted is He had deposited in man, among what He bestowed upon him, a particular subtle quality, which is dignity and the love of greatness and loftiness, whoever places it in its proper place, by being arrogant toward those upon whom God has commanded arrogance, namely the devils of mankind and jinn who disobey Him, is saved, and whoever places it in other than its proper place, by being arrogant toward the friends of God, Lord of Majesty, is destroyed. He, Exalted, made clear that the disbelievers placed it in other than its proper place: ﴿So they said﴾, i.e., all of them said to their messengers, denying with the utmost denial out of arrogance: ﴿Are humans﴾, i.e., this kind, and it is in the nominative as the subject of the verb, because the interrogative demands a verb. Since denying the plural is greater, and had He used the singular pronoun it would not have had the awe of the plural, He said: ﴿guiding us﴾. So they denied the Supreme King's sending of them, ﴿and they disbelieved﴾ by that, immediately after the messengers' coming and because of it, without reflection, thought, or even slight consideration and insight, out of envy of the messengers because they were equal to them in humanity. So they found it improbable that He should single out any matter from among them, especially if it was very great. Thus they were compelled to commit the most hideous act, which is to find it improbable that a prophet should be human while accepting that God could be a stone. ﴿And they turned away﴾, i.e., they imposed upon themselves what the original nature calls against, namely turning away from the messengers after denying their mission, due to a doubt that arose in their minds. This was because they said: God is great and does not resemble humans, so His messengers should be of other than humankind. Had they reflected with due reflection, they would have known that this was not so, and that the messengers are only angels. But since not all humans can bear to see angels, as the greatness they imagined would require, and they did not establish it in its proper form, God, Glorified be He, chose from among humans some people, namely the prophets, peace be upon them, giving them extra powers with which He enabled them to deal with them, so they came to them to be an intermediary between God and His creation, because some of a kind are more inclined to and more receptive to others.

Since all of this is only for the benefit of creation, and no benefit returns to God, Glorified and Exalted, whose majesty is great, from His existence, nor does harm reach Him from anyone's non-existence, and not vice versa, He drew attention to this by His saying: ﴿And God is free of need﴾, i.e., the act of the Supreme King, to whom no one has any command. It is the act of one who seeks independence from them, and He brought them into being in a great manner from among those whom He guided to follow the messengers. So He turned away from them when they turned away from His messengers, and their turning away harmed them, while their turning away did not harm Him. They harmed only themselves. He made the independence absolute so that it would encompass everything.

Since expressing it in this way may give the impression that something came into being that was not previously there, He negated that with His saying, showing additional greatness: ﴿And God﴾, i.e., the one who combines all attributes of perfection without being restricted by any particular aspect, ﴿is Free of need﴾ from all creation, ﴿Praiseworthy﴾, possessing the attribute of absolute independence and the most eloquent praise, which is encompassing all attributes of perfection (p-115), for Him is permanence, without beginning and without end. Nothing has newly come to Him that did not exist before.

When he had established the obligation of believing in Him, His messengers, His books, and the divine decree (al-qadar) in its good and its evil, and had divided people into believers and disbelievers, and had informed us that the disbeliever is arrogant toward the messengers, He specified the greatest cause of their disbelief in His saying, indicating the obligation of believing in the unseen and abandoning speculation (al-qiyas, analogy) and opinion (al-ra'y), since human reason cannot independently grasp some matters of the divine. He expressed this with a word that is most often used for what is doubtful and is also used for falsehood, to indicate that they are doubters even though they are certain, because they have no proof, and that in reality they are in the wrong: ﴿Those who disbelieve claim﴾. Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with both of them, said: "It is the kunya (euphemistic epithet) of falsehood." In the hadith of Abu Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, in Abu Dawud: "Evil is the mount of a man: 'They claimed.'" ﴿Those who disbelieve﴾ [at-Tahrim: 7], that is, they veiled what reason indicates of the oneness of Allah, the Exalted, even at its lowest level.

Since zaʿm (claim) means the assertion of knowledge, and it is a verb that takes two objects, He, glorified is He, placed in their position the clause ﴿that they will never be resurrected﴾ [meaning: that there is no raiser of them from any cause in any way whatsoever]. Since He, glorified is He, had indicated through the two categories of believer and disbeliever the decisive, necessary proof of the existence of the Truth, from which it necessarily follows that He has the Resurrection, He suffices, in the matter of answering them, with His saying [the following]: ﴿Say﴾, that is, to them: ﴿Yes﴾, that is, you will certainly be resurrected. Then He emphasized it with explicit oath, saying: ﴿By my Lord﴾, that is, the One who does good to me (p-116) by avenging Himself upon those who denied Me, by establishing every truth I cause to die and by nullifying every falsehood I raise up, ﴿you will certainly be resurrected﴾. By building the verb in the passive, He indicates that it will occur in a manner of compulsion upon them, with the easiest thing and the simplest matter. Likewise His saying: ﴿Then you will surely be informed﴾, that is, you will certainly be informed with a great informing by the one whom Allah appoints to inform you ﴿of what you did﴾, in order to be recompensed for it. He explained part of what the building of the two verbs in the passive conveys with His saying: ﴿And that﴾, that is, this great matter for you, of resurrection and reckoning, ﴿for Allah﴾, that is, the One encompassing the attributes of perfection alone, ﴿is easy﴾, owing to the acceptance of the material and the availability of power, and the fact that His power, glorified is He, is of this nature: its relation to all possible things, the magnificent and the insignificant alike, is on one and the same footing.

ولَمّا كانَ في رَدِّ قَوْلِهِمْ عَلى هَذا الوَجْهِ مَعَ الإقْسامِ مِن غَيْرِ اسْتِدْلالٍ إشارَةً إلى تَأمُّلِ الكَلامِ السّابِقِ بِما اشْتَمَلَ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ الأدِلَّةِ الَّتِي مِنها ذَلِكَ البُرْهانُ البَدِيهِيُّ، سَبَّبَ عَنْهُ قَوْلُهُ *fadhlaka* (a recapitulative summary) لِما مَضى مِنَ الأدِلَّةِ وجَمْعًا لِحَدِيثِ جِبْرِيلَ عَلَيْهِ الصَّلاةُ والسَّلامُ في الإيمانِ بِاللَّهِ ومَلائِكَتِهِ وكُتُبِهِ ورُسُلِهِ واليَوْمِ الآخِرِ والقَدَرِ خَيْرِهِ وشَرِّهِ والإسْلامِ والإحْسانِ: ﴿فَآمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ﴾ أيِ الَّذِي لا أظْهَرَ مِن أنَّ لَهُ الإحاطَةَ الكامِلَةَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ وأنَّهُ لا كُفُؤَ لَهُ ولا رادَّ لِأمْرِهِ. ولَمّا دَعاهُ هَذا إلى الإيمانِ بِهِ سُبْحانَهُ عَقْلًا ونَقْلًا ذَكَرًا وفِكْرًا، ثَنّى بِالإيمانِ بِالرُّسُلِ مِنَ المَلائِكَةِ والبَشَرِ فَقالَ: ﴿ورَسُولِهِ﴾ أيْ كُلُّ مَن أرْسَلَهُ [و]لا سِيَّما مُحَمَّدٌ (ﷺ) (p-117) بِما ثَبَتَ مِن تَصْدِيقِهِ بِالمُعْجِزاتِ مِن أنَّهُ رَسُولُهُ، ويَلْزَمُ مِنَ الإيمانِ بِهِ الإيمانُ بِمَن أبْلَغَهُ مِنَ المَلائِكَةِ. ولَمّا كانَتْ تِلْكَ المُعْجِزاتُ مُوجِباتٍ لِلْعِلْمِ كانَتْ أحَقَّ الأشْياءِ بِاسْمِ *al-tawr* (light) فَإنَّ النُّورَ هو المَظْهَرُ لِلْأشْياءِ بَعْدَ انْحِجابِها بِرِداءِ الظَّلامِ وكانَ أعْظَمَ تِلْكَ المُعْجِزاتِ وأحَقَّها بِذَلِكَ كُتُبُ اللَّهِ المُنَزَّلَةُ عَلى أنْبِيائِهِ عَلَيْهِمُ الصَّلاةُ والسَّلامُ، وأعْظَمُها القُرْآنُ الَّذِي هو مَعَ إعْجازِهِ بَيانٌ لِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ، قالَ: ﴿والنُّورِ﴾ وعَيَّنَهُ بِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿الَّذِي أنْـزَلْنا﴾ أيْ بِما لَنا مِنَ العَظَمَةِ فَكانَ مُعْجِزًا فَكانَ بِإعْجازِهِ ظاهِرًا بِنَفْسِهِ مُظْهِرًا لِغَيْرِهِ، وهَذا وإنْ كانَ [هُوَ] الواقِعُ لَكِنَّ ذِكْرَ هَذا الوَصْفِ صالِحٌ لِشُمُولِ كُلِّ ما أوْحاهُ اللَّهُ سُبْحانَهُ وتَعالى إلى رُسُلِهِ (ﷺ)، ومِنَ المَعْلُومِ أنَّ أعْظَمَهُ القُرْآنُ المُنَزَّلُ عَلى أشْرَفِ رُسُلِهِ (ﷺ) وعَلَيْهِمْ أجْمَعِينَ، فَهو أحَقُّ ذَلِكَ بِاسْمِ النُّورِ لِما مَضى مِن إعْجازِهِ، فَمَن آمَنَ بِهِ أدْخَلَ اللَّهُ قَلْبَهُ مِن أنْوارِ الفُهُومِ والألْطافِ والسَّكِينَةِ ما يُضِيءُ الأقْطارَ.

ولَمّا كانَ التَّقْدِيرُ: واللَّهُ مُحاسِبُكم عَلى ما قابَلْتُمْ بِهِ إنْعامَهُ عَلَيْكم بِذَلِكَ مِن إيمانٍ وكُفْرانٍ، عُطِفَ عَلَيْهِ مُرَغِّبًا مُرَهِّبًا قَوْلَهُ: ﴿واللَّهُ﴾ أيِ المُحِيطُ عِلْمًا وقُدْرَةً، وقَدَّمَ الجارَّ لِما تَقَدَّمَ غَيْرَ مَرَّةً مِن مَزِيدِ التَّأْكِيدِ فَقالَ: ﴿بِما تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ أيْ تُوقِعُونَ عَمَلَهُ في وقْتٍ مِنَ الأوْقاتِ (p-118) ﴿خَبِيرٌ﴾ أيْ بالِغُ العِلْمِ بِباطِنِهِ وظاهِرِهِ.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 64, verse 9:

When He had informed of the Resurrection and sworn to it, and had pointed to its earlier proof, and had made its consequence the thing that saves on that Day, He mentioned His Day and what happens in it, so as to warn. He said, following what preceded of the pillars of faith, the pillar of the Last Day, admonishing him who says, "Would that I knew what my state will be after my departure," and subduing him who says, "There is no state after departure." This is by informing that they are states, that is, states that turn children grey, break the backs of men, and crush the lofty mountains. ﴿The Day﴾, that is, you will be raised on a Day when ﴿He gathers you﴾, that is, O you two weighty creatures. Since the time by which an action is dated is mentioned only for the sake of what occurs in it, it becomes as if it were the cause of that action, so He, exalted, said: ﴿For the Day of Gathering﴾, for the sake of what happens on that [Day] in which He gathers the people of the heavens and the people of the earth, of reckoning and recompense. It will be a success for some, so they will be the winners, and a loss for others, so they will be the losers. Each of them seeks to be a winner.

Since this aim is a great matter whose mention cuts the hearts, He, exalted, said, pointing to its awfulness with the distal demonstrative, resuming: ﴿That﴾, that is, the great Day of lofty station and sublime attributes, ﴿is the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain﴾, in which there is in reality no mutual loss and gain other than it, because of its magnitude and permanence. Ghabn (loss) is the manifestation of deficiency in one's share arising from something hidden, because on it the First and the Last and all creation are gathered together, and hearing and sight will be to a degree that cannot be described, such that everything that occurs in it can be perceived by everyone of that gathering. Whoever is disgraced is disgraced before all. No servant enters Paradise but he is shown his seat in the Fire, had he done evil, so that he increases in gratitude, and no servant enters the Fire but he is shown his seat in Paradise, had he done good, so that he increases in regret. Thus every unbeliever is a loser by abandoning faith, and every believer is a loser by his shortcoming in goodness. The root *gh-b-n* revolves around concealment, from the *maghabin* of the body, which are the parts hidden from the eye. Ghabn in sale was so named because it is hidden from its owner. The unbeliever and the wrongdoer think that they are cheating the believer of the worldly bounty that the unbeliever monopolised, and of the deficiency the wrongdoer imposed on the wronged. In truth, however, the believer and the wronged one have cheated them both of the bliss of the Hereafter and its great, lasting, complete reward. So the loss on that Day is unlike any other loss. Mentioning this Day in this manner has urged toward taqwa (God-consciousness) in the most complete way. It is what carries one to follow the commands and avoid the prohibitions, lest loss be incurred through the forfeiting or diminishing of bliss, and after that there comes for the unbeliever the painful punishment.

Since everyone supposes that he will be in the light, dislikes being in darkness, loves to be a winner, and dislikes to be a loser, the preceding and following words indicated the implied sense: whoever believed will be in the light, and on that Day, by the heaviness of his scale, he will be among the winners; whoever disbelieved will be in darkness, and on that Day, by the lightness of his scale, he will be among the losers. So He joined to this His saying, explaining the effects of that loss and giving precedence to it by mending what carries one to taqwa. Among these are the cognitive faculty: ﴿And whoever believes﴾, that is, he brings about faith and renews it continually, ﴿in God﴾, that is, the Supreme King, to whom there is no equal. Since He mentioned the head, which is the rectifying of the cognitive faculty, He followed it with the body, which is the rectifying of the practical faculty, and said: ﴿and does righteousness﴾, confirming his faith, ﴿righteous deeds﴾, that is, deeds worth caring to attain, because there is no equal to them in bringing benefits and repelling harms.

Since the religion, despite its ease, is firm, and no one will oppose it without being overcome, He said, urging toward taqwa by the promise of averting harms, and perhaps He used the singular pronoun to indicate that the time of expiation and entry varies according to the length or brevity of the reckoning; whenever one finishes the reckoning, he enters Paradise if he is among its people: ﴿He will expiate﴾, that is, God, according to the reading of the majority, by covering with a great covering, ﴿from him his misdeeds﴾, which the deficiency of nature overcame him in. He followed this with the other motivator, the inducement that brings gladness, because a person draws near to his Lord, glorified be He, on the two wings of fear and hope, of awe and desire, of warning and good tidings. So He said: ﴿And He will admit him﴾, that is, out of mercy, honour and bounty, ﴿to gardens﴾, that is, orchards with great trees and shady boughs that screen what is within them, and meadows of wide extent, varied in blossoms, fragrant in their scent, delighting the beholder. He indicated the lasting of their irrigation by His saying: ﴿flowing﴾. Since the general presence of water throughout the whole earth is not praiseworthy, He made clear that it is within them in the best of conditions, so He said: ﴿beneath them﴾, and He showed its greatness by saying: ﴿the rivers﴾. Since removal, or the expectation of it, from such a state is distressing, He removed the expectation of that by saying, gathering, lest one suppose that eternity belongs to one particular person, explicitly stating that among its meaning is gathering, and that all who enter it are equal in eternity: ﴿abiding therein﴾. He emphasised this by His saying: ﴿forever﴾. The estimate according to the reading of Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir, with the *nun* (we), is: We shall effect the expiation and the admission into this bliss by the greatness that is ours, for none can grant felicity to whom He wills and misery to whom He wills except God, glorified be He. This power is not perfect except for one who is great, whose command none can ever repel.

Since this is a striking matter whose bliss brings gladness to the heart, He indicated its greatness by that which brings gladness to the heart, saying: ﴿That﴾, that is, the matter of exceeding loftiness of forgiveness and honour, and nothing else, ﴿is the great success﴾, because it comprises all benefits together with the repelling of harms and the bringing of joys. (p-122)

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 64, verse 10:

When he had mentioned the one who succeeds by adhering to taqwa (God-consciousness) as an encouragement, he followed it with the one who fails, by way of warning, because of the corruption of the two faculties that drive one toward taqwa: the cognitive ('ilmiyyah) and the practical ('amaliyyah). He began with the cognitive faculty, saying: ﴿And those who disbelieved﴾, i.e., they covered over the proofs of that Day, so they remained in darkness. When he had mentioned their corruption of the cognitive faculty, he followed it with the practical, saying: ﴿and denied﴾, i.e., they committed all manner of covering over and all manner of denial ﴿Our signs﴾, on account of them, along with their greatness, by attributing them to Us, so they did nothing [of good].

When he had explained their corruption of the two faculties, he threatened them with harms, saying, omitting the fa' (so-then) on both sides, the wretched and the happy, as a dropping of causes, because the focus of this surah is more on the innate natures, in which no other has any part, with his saying: ﴿He it is who created you, and among you is a disbeliever and among you is a believer﴾ [al-Taghabun: 2]. For that is more worthy of fear, so that one is more worthy of distancing oneself from what indicates a corrupt nature, namely evil deeds: ﴿Those﴾, i.e., the distant, the hateful, ﴿are the companions of the Fire.﴾ Since imprisonment, when release from it is hoped for, lessens the fear of one within it, and since expressing it with "companionship" indicates permanence, which cuts the hearts because it is without hope of release, he emphasized it with his saying: ﴿abiding therein forever﴾, and he increased the terror of it (p-123) with his saying, [indicating] the harms of the heart after mentioning the harms of the body: ﴿and wretched is the destination﴾, i.e., all the blameworthy qualities are gathered in the destination toward it and in the place which is for arriving at it. How then with it being a dwelling for a long time, and how much more so when it is on the basis of eternal abiding.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 64, verse 11:

Since it is among His ways of making Himself known, to those who encourage and those who warn, that He does this only regarding what is not within the power of the one who acts to preserve and control, so that the doer does not need a watcher to guard it or a guardian who is bound to that work and controls it, and since the statement of the hypocrites mentioned earlier concerned spending and calamities, and calamities are made easier to bear when they come from the Beloved, He said, answering one who imagines a lack of power, completing what has passed concerning the character of deeds by belief in the divine decree (qadar), its good and its evil, encouraging submission, warning against impatient distress, and restricting the verb so that it covers every object: ﴿No calamity befalls﴾, that is, no one upon whom calamities can possibly descend, and He mentioned the verb to indicate its power, and He intensified the negation with His words ﴿except a calamity﴾, that is, a calamity whether it was religious or worldly, from disbelief or other than it, ﴿except by the permission of Allah﴾, that is, by the decree and empowerment of the Supreme King. So no believer should let anything of that hinder him from the beneficial piety on the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain (yawm al-taghabun).

Since a cause of that was implied, its estimated sense being: ﴿And whoever disbelieves in Allah﴾, by His decree upon him, (p-124) disbelief, ﴿He will guide his heart astray﴾, and increase him in misguidance, so he does what drives him deeper into calamity until they become many calamities and destroy him, He joined to it His words, prompting the first pillar of Islam, which is the reform of the cognitive faculty: ﴿And whoever believes in Allah﴾, that is, faith is found at some time and renews itself through the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, by the cause of the Supreme King, His decree and His permission, ﴿He guides his heart﴾, that is, He increases him in guidance through what He renews for him of success at every time, until his faith becomes firmly rooted, so every calamity is removed from him, for he remembers that it is from Allah and that what befell him would not have missed him, and what missed him would not have befallen him. So he submits to His decree, is patient regarding it, and does and says what Allah and His Messenger commanded, and it becomes light for him, and nothing hinders him from any of the means of salvation on the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain. Rather, through these he gains many profits and benefits, so his life becomes good with comprehensive well-being in the religious and the worldly matters, because through well-being in worldly matters life is made good in [this world, and through well-being in religious matters life is made good in -] the Hereafter, so that the life is pleasing. This happens when his deeds become right in his times of happiness and hardship, so he abandons every religious and bodily grave sin and every inward sin of the heart, and abandons panic at worldly calamities, such as fear, hunger, loss of wealth, lives and fruits. (p-125) This is because when the heart is sound, the whole body is made sound.

Since the implied sense was the reason for that: ﴿So Allah is All-Powerful over everything﴾, [He - ] leaves nothing to occur except by His permission, He joined to it His words: ﴿And Allah﴾, that is, the King who has no peer, ﴿is All-Knowing of everything﴾ absolutely, without any qualification. So when whoever Allah guided realizes this, every false belief is removed, whether disbelief, innovation, or any corrupt trait.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 64, verse 12:

Since the implied sense is: patience in the face of the onslaught of calamities, he (Allah) followed it with His words, as a warning against becoming preoccupied with them [so that one falls into ruin, is cut off from the means of salvation, and indicating the learning of the matters of religion from its opponents], pointing out that worship is not accepted except by following (ittiba', adherence to the prophetic model) and not by innovating (ibtida', introducing what is not from the religion): ﴿And obey Allah﴾, that is, the Supreme King to whom all command belongs. So do in every calamity and misfortune that befalls you and every matter that besets you what He has legislated for you. He emphasized it by repeating the verb, indicating that standing at the limits, especially at times of calamity, is extremely difficult, so He said: ﴿And obey the Messenger﴾, that is, the one perfect in messengership, ﷺ. He is the one protected (ma'sum) by what He created in him of moderation (i'tidal), [and] by what He purified him with, of the splitting of the belly and the washing of the heart several times, and by what He strengthened him with of revelation. Thus, actions are moderate when they are guided by reason, together with obedience to Allah and following His Messenger ﷺ in every advance and retreat, whether they are appetitive or irascible. When they are not like this (p-126) they deviate upward or downward, and thus they are blameworthy. Indeed, Allah the Exalted, by the subtlety of His management, composed in the human being an irascible power that repels what destroys and harms him, and an appetitive power that attracts what nourishes and strengthens him. The moderation of the irascible power is courage, its deficiency is cowardice, and its excess is recklessness. Thus people, according to it, are coward, brave, and reckless. The moderation of the appetitive power is chastity, its deficiency is asceticism, and its excess is greed. People, according to it, are ascetic, chaste, and greedy. Both extremes of the paths of conduct are blameworthy, and the scale of justice is following the Messenger ﷺ in what he legislated. By that, the apparent and hidden trials are removed, and there is no path to Allah except by what He legislated. Every path He did not legislate is error, from disbelief to whatever it records. Then he connected to His command this statement, expressing it with the particle of doubt (in fa-in, "but if"), indicating good news of the preservation of this community from apostasy, and suggesting that some of them may fall into that, and then their return or destruction is near: ﴿But if you turn away﴾, that is, you burden yourselves, when the first natural disposition calls you to turn away from this greatest light and to incline toward one of the extremes understood from the two extremes of moderation, then there is nothing upon Our Messenger concerning your turning away. ﴿Then upon Our Messenger is only﴾, he attributed it to Himself in the form of majesty, glorifying him and threatening whoever turns away from him: ﴿the clear conveyance﴾ (p-127), that is, the evident one in himself, making manifest to everyone that he made it extremely clear to them and left no ambiguity. The creation of guidance in hearts is not his responsibility.

When this was distressing, because it implies their turning away while there was no means of turning them back, it was made known that this is only up to Him, and [that He is] the One able to do it. So He said, in answer to one who seems to have said, "What is the remedy for their affair," completing the two divisions of religion (worship and seeking help) after stating the other division, which is worship: ﴿Allah﴾, that is, the One encompassing all attributes of perfection, ﴿there is no god but Him﴾. He is the One able to turn them towards [Himself], and no other can do that. So refuge is to Him in every repelling and every gaining, and He is the One sought for help in every matter. So let those who seek guidance seek it from Him regarding their guidance. ﴿And upon Allah﴾, that is, the One to whom the whole matter belongs, not upon anyone else.

Since [absolute] faith is affirming Allah by believing that He is able to do everything, so that no one has any command alongside Him and no one is equal to Him, how much more so is firmness in it. He drew attention to this requirement with the connecting fa' and the emphasis of the imperative lam (lam al-amr) in His saying: ﴿So let the believers rely [upon Allah]﴾, meaning that reliance should come into being in a form that is at the height of clarity and steadfastness. The steadfast ones in this attribute, in turning back whoever turns away from among them if that occurs, and likewise in every absent matter, are the ones who have the highest share in every reliance. Chastity is not specific to what is present; just as the rule of justice regarding what is present is obedience, the rule of justice regarding what is absent is reliance. Likewise was the conduct of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, and they had the greatest share in every (p-128) reliance, especially when the Arabs apostatised after the death of the Prophet (ﷺ). The one most worthy of this attribute was al-Siddiq (Abu Bakr), may Allah be pleased with him, as is known to whoever examines the books composed on the biographies (siyar) and the reports of the apostasy (ridda), especially my book entitled on the reports of the apostasy.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 64, verse 14:

Since the commands of the religion are sometimes considered with regard to the religious command, [that is,] among the purely devotional acts of obedience, and sometimes with regard to the creational command (al-amr al-takwini), which is what comes through wealth, family or children, Allah, glory be to Him, completed the first division in the two preceding verses. He then began on the second command, because it may give rise to a trial in religion and it may give rise to a trial in this world. Since the trial of being occupied with it or turning away from it is the greatest of trials, because it separates a man from his spouse and a man from his son, and makes a close friend forget his close friend, as was witnessed at the beginning of Islam, and the greatest of that was in apostasy (ridda), and the prohibition against being diverted by wealth and children had already preceded, and the prohibition regarding children was a prohibition regarding spouses by way of priority, therefore He restricted it to them (the children) without the spouses. And since the one commanded to rely on God (tawakkul) might think that surrendering his reins to everyone does not harm reliance on God, He pointed out that the structure of this abode upon means (al-asbab) prevents that, and so He commanded with something like "tie it and rely on God" and "strive for what benefits you, seek help from God, and do not feel helpless," the hadith. So He said, in answer to that, for one who needs to ask about the like of it, clarifying the commands with regard to the creational test, although the people most entitled to exert effort in disciplining, correcting and refining him are the closest of relatives and the people most attached to a person (p-١٢٩) and it serves as the cause for another matter in "The Hypocrites": ﴿O you who have believed﴾. And since spouses are closer in enmity than children, He put them first, saying, emphasizing it for one who finds that far-fetched: ﴿Indeed, among your spouses﴾, even if they show the utmost affection, ﴿and your children﴾, even if they also show the utmost compassion and tenderness, ﴿are an enemy to you﴾, that is, because they occupy you away from religion, or for other reasons such as gathering wealth and seeking status for their sake, and neglecting the forbidding of wrongdoing; for a child is a cause of cowardice, and other reasons. Abu Hayyan, may God have mercy on him, said: "No one is more hostile to a man than his spouse and child when they are enemies, and that is in this world and the hereafter. In this world, by the ruin of his wealth, as is well known, and his honor. In the hereafter, by what he strives to acquire of the unlawful for their sake, and by what they earn from it through his status."

So the man who sees that as a blessing from God and makes them helpers for him in His obedience, not cutters-off and obstacles from what pleases Him, by [not being distracted] by their love, their enmity and their hatred. When He reported the enmity, He expressed it in a way that may be understood by one person only, for lightness. And when He commanded caution, [He gathered it, as an indication of increasing warning and fear regarding everyone, even if they are the closest of relatives, because prudence is suspicion of others, as al-Tabarani narrated in al-Awsat. So He based on the report of enmity the command of caution] in His saying: ﴿So beware of them﴾, that is, by being mindful of God in all their affairs, so that in striving for them you seek only what is sufficient and lawful, and do not let your love for them lead you to anything else; and let your caution from them be intensified by acting on what God has commanded, even in justice among them, lest they gain power to harm you, for then the matter would grow grave with them and they would become a trial for you in religion, either by apostasy, God forbid, or by being preoccupied away from obedience, or by plunging into disobedience and opposing the Sunnah and the community.

Since harm may befall one despite caution, because caution does not avert what is decreed, or [it may befall one] despite submission, and since entrusting the one who harms to God is more fitting and greater in seeking help, He said, guiding to that: ﴿And if you pardon﴾, that is, you forgo punishing them for their sins by not inflicting punishment for them, for there is no benefit in that, because whoever has been sealed upon something does not return; what is beneficial is the cautious one to whom He, glory be to Him, has pointed, lest it become a cause of the blame that is forbidden.

And since giving up one's shares is very difficult, He emphasized, glory be to Him, saying: ﴿and overlook﴾, that is, by turning away from retaliating with reproach by the tongue, ﴿and forgive﴾ [that is], by concealing their sins with a complete concealment encompassing both the eye and the trace, by overlooking after abandoning punishment, and leaving blame, so that there is no preoccupation on your part with enmity toward them, nor anything that may drag you from what benefits you of obedience. And since the implication was: God will forgive you, He based on it His saying: ﴿Indeed, God﴾, that is, the one who combines the attributes of perfection, ﴿is Forgiving﴾, that is, reaching (p-١٣١) the erasure of the very traces of sins, and preferring them as a reward for you for your forgiving them. He is worthy of setting them right for you because of your forgiving them, for He is ﴿Merciful﴾; after that concealment He increases you in honor with bounty if you honor them. So adopt His attributes, glory be to Him, and He will increase you of His bounty.

The conclusion of the discussion (of the earlier part) is that when He passed judgment on some of them, it was as if it were said: "What is the ruling on the rest of them?" Thus the ruling on that implies caution regarding all of them. However, stating it explicitly has a great secret in the soul's inclination toward it. So He said, encompassing all of them and including with them the wealth by which all of that subsists, and placing it first because it is the greater trial: ﴿Indeed﴾. He omitted the preposition because none of that is free from occupying the heart. So He said: ﴿Your wealth﴾, meaning in general, ﴿and your children﴾ likewise, ﴿are a trial﴾, meaning a test that inclines you away from God. He knows better than you what is in your souls, but so that there may appear in the world of witnessing (the visible world) who is inclined by it, and it becomes a vengeance upon him, while for one who is not inclined by it, it becomes a blessing. Often a person seeks the wellbeing of his wealth and his child, so he exaggerates and thereby corrupts his own soul, and then that does not set right his wealth or his child. That is because it is part of its nature to drive one to gain what is unlawful, to withhold the right, and to fall into sin. It is narrated from Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah, in the biography of Sufyan al-Thawri, from him that he said: "A man will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and it will be said to him: 'His dependants have eaten up his good deeds.'" And the trial of wealth is sufficiently illustrated by the story of Tha'labah ibn Hatib, one of those concerning whom the saying of the Exalted was revealed: ﴿And among them are those who covenanted with God, "If He gives us of His bounty, we will surely give charity"﴾ [al-Tawbah: 75]. It seems that He, glorified be He, omitted mention of spouses from the trial, because among them are some who are a righteous support toward the Hereafter.

Since the sense was: in guarding against their trials there is great hardship, and by it one gains from them only a small share, and the soul tends to recoil when it abandons what is doubtful and what it loves, He followed it with a word that makes it easier for him, by pointing out that this (worldly gain) is perishing, while for it He has promised a reward that bears no comparison to it, given that the reward endures. His saying: ﴿And God﴾, meaning the Lord of Majesty, ﴿with Him﴾, and sufficient is what comes from Him by way of His majesty and greatness, ﴿is a reward﴾. And God, glorified be He, did not rely on the context to show that the nunation (in ajrun) is for magnification, but further described it by His saying: ﴿great﴾, meaning for whoever complies with His commands, whose benefit returns only to its doer. So he does not prefer anything over His pleasure, neither wealth nor child. That reward is greater than the benefit you would gain from your wealth and children in a way that diminishes obedience.

The Qur'an verse ﴿Fa-ttaqu Allah﴾ is the closing summary (fadhlaka) of what preceded in the whole surah. Since the sense was: "and with Him is a painful punishment for whoever opposes," its consequence is His saying: ﴿So fear God (taqwa)﴾, stated explicitly rather than in pronoun form, to magnify the position and to guard against the thought that a particular kind of taqwa is meant. The explicit wording conveys that the meaning is: make between yourselves and the wrath of the Most High King a shield (wiqaya), without regard to any particular aspect or specific matter, by avoiding His prohibitions after complying with His commands. For taqwa, when it stands alone, is meant to include both doing the commands and abandoning the prohibitions. (p-133) When it is joined with something else, it means only avoiding the prohibitions.

Since the matter, when attributed to Him, Glory be to Him, is greater than any speaker's statement, and no one can estimate Him as He deserves, He lightened and eased it with His saying: ﴿as much as you are able﴾, meaning: as long as you are in general able and capable, and the obligation (taklif) is directed at you in matters of knowledge and action. Exert your effort in this regarding matters of faith, concerning what you know of His essence, rank, attributes, and actions, the Exalted, and in all your other deeds, outward and inward. The greatest of these is emigration (hijra) and striving (jihad). So let your inclination toward them not prevent you, and let taqwa regarding what of the disliked matters has occurred be through regret and ceasing, together with the resolve not to return to it; and regarding what has not occurred, through guarding against its causes. When a person exerts all his effort, that is taqwa "as is due to Him." Thus there is no abrogation (naskh), and God knows best.

Since manifesting Islam involves hardship, like the deeds, He said: ﴿and listen﴾, meaning, listen with submission and acceptance to what you are admonished with and to all His commands. ﴿And obey﴾, meaning, and confirm that submission by actually carrying out the outward acts of Islam, through upholding God's command and showing compassion toward God's creatures in every command and prohibition, according to capacity. The object is omitted so that the command is fulfilled by every act of obedience, whether whole or partial; and likewise regarding spending. Since spending is difficult, He emphasized its command by singling it out for mention, saying: ﴿and spend﴾, meaning, carry out spending as He has set it for you, in what He has made obligatory or recommended, even if it is toward someone from whom you have discovered enmity. Spending is not restricted to one kind but includes what God has provided, both the personal (dhati) and the external (khariji).

Since what drives stinginess is what comes to mind of the necessities, the most precious of which is the necessity of one's own self, He encouraged it by what first comes to mind and encompasses all that preceded, saying: ﴿good﴾, meaning, let that be the greatest good that occurs, ﴿for yourselves﴾. For God gives better than it in this world, by which the self is purified, and stores up for it in the Hereafter reward whose reality one does not know. So let no immediate thing of that deceive you, for it is merely ornament and delusion with no real substance.

When He mentioned the good in spending, He generalized it to all commands, saying: ﴿And whoever is protected﴾, constructed in the passive to magnify the encouragement toward it, with the self made the subject while the helper is removed from the agent, meaning: whoever is shielded by any shield whatsoever. He attributed it to ﴿the stinginess of his self﴾, in which all evil lies. So he acts with his wealth and with everything he is commanded, doing what he is able of what he was commanded, certain of it and at peace with it, until the disturbances are lifted from his heart, and he guards himself against the bondage of created things. Stinginess (shuhh) is an inner disposition, the chronic disease, the head of the serpent, and every trial is misguidance. Miserliness (bukhl) is an outward act that arises from stinginess. The self sometimes is stingy by withholding the desire from sins and so commits them, and sometimes by giving its limbs to acts of obedience and so abandons them, and sometimes by spending wealth. (p-135) Whoever does what is obligatory upon him has left stinginess behind.

Since the one who shields is only God, the Exalted, He made His shielding the cause for His saying: ﴿those﴾, meaning the people of high rank, ﴿they are﴾, meaning exclusively, ﴿the successful﴾, meaning those who have attained all their desires through what they feared God in, of worldly matters, such as wealth, children, family, and all the distracting hindrances of every obstacle.

When he had commanded and warned against the opposite in a general way, he encouraged spending, emphasizing his command, because it (spending) is difficult, especially in the time of the Prophet (ﷺ), for wealth was then extremely precious, and especially if it was among the necessities of women, whom the surah began by stating that some of them are enemies, and especially if the enmity was openly manifest. So He said, explaining success, gently inviting them through the expression of lending, and indicating with the particle of doubt that it is contrary to natural inclination: ﴿If you lend to God﴾, that is, to the Sovereign Most High, the One of absolute self-sufficiency who combines all attributes of perfection, by spending wealth and all your strength, which He made a trial for you in His obedience. He encouraged benevolence in it by sincerity and other means, so He said: ﴿a goodly loan﴾, that is, in the manner of sincerity and promptness, and placing it in its best positions in the easiest, most beautiful, most wholesome and most just ways. The greatest encouragement to it is that He arranged upon it profit in this world and forgiveness in the Hereafter, so He said: ﴿He will multiply it for you﴾, that is, for your sake specifically, at least tenfold for one, (p-136) up to what has no end, according to the intentions. Al-Qushayri said: this address is directed at the rich in the expenditure of their wealth, and at the poor in emptying their days and times of their own desires and preferring the desire of the Truth over the desire of their souls. So the rich is told: prefer My command over your desire in your wealth [and other than it], and the poor is told: prefer My rule in your self, your heart and your time.

Since man, with his deficiencies, however much he strives, cannot reach all that he is commanded, because the religion, though easy, is firm, ("Whoever overburdens himself in this religion will be overcome by it"), He said: ﴿And He will forgive you﴾, that is, He brings about forgiveness, which is the erasure of what was neglected, its trace and its effect, for your sake, through the blessing of spending. These two clauses comprise the bringing of joy and the repelling of evils, and that is all of happiness.

Since the estimate was: then God is Forgiving and Forbearing, He conjoined to it His saying: ﴿And God﴾, that is, whose greatness cannot be measured [by anything], ﴿is All-Appreciative﴾, that is, abundant in gratitude toward whoever gives for His sake, even if it is little, so He rewards him with a great reward beyond counting, and this looks to the multiplication. ﴿Forbearing﴾, who does not hasten to punish for any sin, however great it may be, but rather gives long and ample respite so that the servant may remember the kindness together with the disobedience and repent. He does not neglect, nor should one be deceived by His forbearance, for the anger of the Forbearing is unbearable, (p-137) and this returns to forgiveness.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 64, verse 18:

Since the forbearing (al-halim) may be suspected, in his forbearance, of being attributed to ignorance of the sin or of its magnitude, He said: ﴿Knower of the unseen﴾, which is what is hidden from all of creation, so it includes what is within the heart of the kind of things that natural disposition brings about and which the possessor of the heart has no knowledge of, let alone others. And since one might think that knowledge of what is hidden does not necessitate knowledge of what is witnessed, or think that knowledge relates only to universals, He said, clarifying that His knowledge of the worlds, both universals and particulars, before existence and after it, is on an equal footing: ﴿and the witnessed﴾, which is everything that has become manifest, so that creation knows it. This attribute calls to ihsan (excellence) in that it obliges the believer to abandon the outward and inward of the sin, and every shortcoming, slackness, heedlessness and negligence, so that he worships Allah as though he sees Him.

When that encompassed everything hidden from creation and everything not hidden from them, nothing remained except that one might imagine that the delay of punishment is due to incapacity, so He said: ﴿the Mighty﴾, meaning the One who overcomes everything and is not overcome by anything. And since that might be due to another matter for which He is not praised, He said: ﴿the Wise﴾, meaning that He delayed it only for a far-reaching wisdom which creatures are unable to comprehend. He has set creatures in obedience to Him by their running under His will; at times this coincides with His command and is called obedience, and at times it opposes it and is called disobedience. So whoever He wills to complete His blessing upon by granting success in obedience, by conforming to His command with the encompassing of His knowledge and perfection in His management through His far-reaching wisdom, and continuing that and preserving it from every calamity through His dazzling might; and whoever He wills to withhold that from, likewise. All of it is glorification of Him, subhanahu, by indicating that He is the One, the Subduer. He has encompassed the beginning of the Friday (sura) with this surah, its beginning and its end, so this one came explaining it and revealing it in a more magnificent manner, because the aim of this is the outcome of the aim of that. And He has returned, by being exempt from the blemishes of deficiency and by being specified with all the attributes of perfection, and the comprehensiveness of power for the truth, and the encompassing of knowledge of the states of the disbeliever and the believer, to the opening of it the goodness of its closing; and He knew manifestly the grandeur of its arrangement, and the wondrousness of the harmony of all its verses and the brilliance of their cohesion. And Allah is the Granter of success to what is right.
